Deleting a category referenced by a host leaves a dangling category_id, breaking TopicEmbed.import's `category: eh.try(:category_id)` and the admin UI rendering. This is a real data-integrity defect in the diff.

judged_text: category_id is created as a bare integer with no foreign key and no dependent/nullify hook, so deleting the referenced category leaves embeddable_hosts rows pointing at a nonexistent category. An admin who deletes a category that embeddable hosts post to leaves dangling rows: the admin UI renders a blank category badge and TopicEmbed.import passes the dead category_id to PostCreator, so new embeds for that host break or land in an invalid category.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `embeddable_hosts.category_id` as a required integer column (`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`) with `belongs_to :category` (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`), but there is no foreign key constraint and no model/database behavior to nullify/reassign hosts when a category is deleted. If a referenced category is removed, `host.category` can become `nil` (template uses `{{category-badge host.category}}`), and `TopicEmbed.import` will still pass `eh.try(:category_id)` to `PostCreator` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`), potentially using an ID that no longer exists. The exact failure mode inside `PostCreator` isn't shown in the diff, so the “break” claim can't be fully verified, but the dangling-reference risk is real and grounded in the changes.
